active_subtask: Phase C: NPU offload crash ROOT-CAUSED AND FIXED. ggml-hexagon.cpp hardcodes mmap_support=false; llama.cpp's AUTO load-mode logic disables mmap for the WHOLE model (not just the NPU's share) whenever any device in -dev reports no mmap support, forcing an eager full-file read that blew past available RAM in ~10s. Fix: pass -lm mmap explicitly (bypasses the AUTO-only mmap-disable check). Verified live with full logcat+mem+watchdog instrumentation: -dev HTP0 -lm mmap --n-cpu-moe 48 completed cleanly, no crash, no Scudo error, memory stayed healthy (free 650-760MB, available pinned at 5.5GB throughout) despite peak process RSS of ~6.1GB. Earlier Scudo 'invalid chunk state' crashes were very likely a downstream symptom of the same RSS-explosion/OOM pressure, not a distinct Hexagon kernel bug. hardware_target restored to NPU_CPU_HYBRID. Next: re-run the full Phase C sweep (baseline/APLS/ngram-simple) with -lm mmap as a now-mandatory flag whenever -dev HTP0 is used.

Phase 0: confirmed no true BitNet ternary (1.58-bit) checkpoint exists for Qwen3-Coder-Next; corrected ULBC to REAP pruning + MXFP4/IQ2 post-hoc quantization (Decision D2)
Phase 0: confirmed via Hugging Face connector that Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-Next is a real base model with REAP-pruned and MXFP4_MOE GGUF conversions available

Phase A: surveyed GGUF file sizes across 4 repos/quant families via HF hf_fs; smallest real candidate is mradermacher/Qwen3-Coder-Next-REAP-40B-A3B-i1-GGUF IQ1_S at 7.85 GiB -- still exceeds the 4.2GiB RAM budget as a raw file size; mmap paging behavior must be measured, not assumed, in Phase C
Phase A: verified GGUF metadata via HTTP range request (first 32MiB) + local sparse-file trick (os.truncate to real size) feeding gguf-py's GGUFReader, avoiding full multi-GB downloads

Phase A: CONFIRMED Qwen3-Coder-Next has NO MTP/NextN weights in any checked GGUF (mradermacher REAP-40B i1-IQ1_S and bartowski unpruned IQ1_S both: 48 blocks, 843 tensors, zero nextn.* tensors, no qwen3next.nextn_predict_layers KV key) and no such field in the upstream Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-Next config.json. This is upstream, not a conversion artifact. Decision D4: pillar 3 (MTP) is not usable for this model; fall back to --spec-type ngram-simple.

Phase A: read ggml-hexagon.cpp VTCM-budget code directly: VTCM gates per-op tile size (auto-shrinks, floor at 128 elem/1 row), not NPU-resident capacity. Real ceiling is opt_mbuf (GGML_HEXAGON_MBUF env var), default 1024 MiB max single fastRPC/DMA buffer -- this is the APLS tuning knob, not VTCM. Corrects the Phase 0 guess.
Phase A: picked working candidate -- mradermacher/Qwen3-Coder-Next-REAP-40B-A3B-i1-GGUF, file Qwen3-Coder-Next-REAP-40B-A3B.i1-IQ1_S.gguf
Wrote and committed docs/QWEN3_TRIAD_PLAN.md updates for Phase A findings

Phase B: REVISED Decision D1 -- no separate checkout needed. The existing pinned commit (e358d591, same one install-npu.sh already builds) was confirmed in Phase 0/A to fully support qwen3next/MTP-code-path/n-cpu-moe/MUL_MAT_ID, so running the existing validated install-npu.sh (into .work-npu/, untouched pin files) is strictly better than a second SDK/toolchain setup.

Phase B: dropped OpenCL/GPU from hardware_target -- README already has measured evidence OpenCL is 32.8-66.9% slower than CPU on this device; no reason to carry it into this track. hardware_target changed from HYBRID_NPU_STREAMING to NPU_CPU_HYBRID.

Phase B: started background download of the 7.85GiB candidate GGUF to ~/models/qwen3-coder-next-reap-40b/ (resumable curl, log at curl.log in that dir) to overlap with the build instead of serializing after it
Phase B: GGUF download completed (8426713408 bytes, matches expected size)

Phase B: ./install-npu.sh --jobs 1 completed successfully (~1hr wall clock, overlapped with the download). Binaries at .work-npu/build/bin/{llama-completion,llama-bench,test-backend-ops}. Installer's own DSP matrix validation: 8/8 passed. --list-devices confirms HTP0 (Hexagon) detected.

Phase C: GATE 1 PASSED -- llama-completion loads the real downloaded GGUF and generates coherent (if repetitive) English with --device none (CPU-only): 'The capital of France is what?\nThe capital of France is **' from -n 8. No crash, no OOM. CPU-only perf: 1.46 tok/s prompt, 0.30 tok/s generation -- very slow, likely mmap page-fault bound against the ~4-6GB RAM budget vs 8.4GB file; not yet isolated from pure compute cost.
Phase C: started a longer (-n 48) CPU-only coherence check, same prompt, to judge output quality before any NPU/APLS acceleration tuning

Phase C: coherence check (-n 48) completed -- QUALIFIED PASS. Output: 'The capital of France is which?\nThe capital of France is **Paris**. The Paris is the French government's capital...' then degrades into repeating 'The Paris is the French government's capital.' after ~15-20 tokens. Model gets the fact right and is grammatical early, but loops. Default sampler had repeat_penalty=1.000 (disabled) in this run -- untried lever before giving up on IQ1_S.
Phase C: tested --repeat-penalty 1.3 -- fixed the loop but produced incoherent gibberish (too aggressive)

Phase C: tested --repeat-penalty 1.1 --repeat-last-n 64 -- SWEET SPOT. No loop, correct fact (Paris) retained, coherent prose. VERDICT: IQ1_S REAP-40B-A3B is usable; --repeat-penalty 1.1 --repeat-last-n 64 is now a REQUIRED flag for all subsequent runs (default sampler loops on this model/quant). No fallback to IQ2_XXS needed.
Phase C: CPU-only baseline via llama-bench -dev none -p 64 -n 16 -r 1 -- pp64=6.69 tok/s, tg16=1.21 tok/s. Model confirmed by llama-bench as qwen3next 80B.A3B IQ1_S, 40.99B params.

Phase C: discovered ADSP_LIBRARY_PATH/LD_LIBRARY_PATH must be exported manually when invoking binaries directly (install-npu.sh's npu_runtime() sets these internally but only within its own script chain) -- fixes HTP0 'failed to open session, error 0x80000406'

Phase C: user reported repeated crashes from running -dev HTP0 against the real model; diagnosed via logcat -d -b main -b system -b crash -b events (previously unchecked) -- found Fatal signal 6 (SIGABRT), 'Scudo ERROR: invalid chunk state when deallocating', 11+ reproductions
Phase C: discussed hypothesis with user (MoE active-expert routing moving data 'in pieces' causing corruption) BEFORE any further coding, per explicit user request
Phase C: set up full forensic harness (continuous logcat stream to file, 1s/0.5s memory+process sampler, verbose llama.cpp logging) before re-testing, so a repeat crash would be fully diagnosable

Phase C: ran -dev HTP0 --n-cpu-moe 48 (all MoE forced to CPU, isolating whether crash is MoE-specific) with full instrumentation -- NO Scudo crash this time, but captured a DIFFERENT failure: process RSS ballooned from 19MB to 6.2GB in ~10 seconds (measured via 1s-interval ps samples), available RAM crashed to ~15MB, swap exploded from 1.0GB to 5GB -- a genuine OOM/thrashing death spiral, not heap corruption

Phase C: root-caused via source inspection: llama-model.cpp:1512-1519 disables mmap for the ENTIRE model if ANY device in -dev reports mmap_support=false under AUTO load-mode; ggml-hexagon.cpp:7517 hardcodes mmap_support=false (vs ggml-cpu.cpp's true). This means -dev HTP0 alone (regardless of --n-cpu-moe) forces eager full-file read instead of lazy paging -- explaining the RSS explosion precisely. Likely also explains the earlier Scudo aborts as a downstream symptom of the same memory exhaustion.

Phase C: FIX VERIFIED LIVE with full logcat+mem-monitor+watchdog safety net: -dev HTP0 -lm mmap --n-cpu-moe 48 (forcing mmap explicitly bypasses the AUTO-only disable check) completed cleanly -- load 10.1s, prompt eval 4.00 tok/s, decode eval 2.46 tok/s (better than CPU-only baseline's 1.21 tok/s), zero crashes, zero Scudo errors, memory stable throughout (free 650-760MB, available 5.5GB, peak RSS ~6.1GB but no thrashing). Output was incoherent at this run's settings (temp=0 greedy, no repeat-penalty) -- expected per the earlier coherence findings, orthogonal to the crash fix. -lm mmap is now a REQUIRED flag whenever -dev HTP0 is used.

failed_attempts.what: Any invocation of llama-completion, llama-bench, or test-backend-ops with -dev HTP0 / -b HTP0 against the real qwen3next model (IQ1_S REAP-40B-A3B GGUF) on the Hexagon backend built at pin e358d591.
failed_attempts.error: CONFIRMED via `logcat -d -b main -b system -b crash -b events`: every one of these processes died with Fatal signal 6 (SIGABRT) and abort message 'Scudo ERROR: invalid chunk state when deallocating address 0x...' -- this is Android's hardened allocator detecting HEAP CORRUPTION (a bad/already-freed pointer), not out-of-memory. 100% reproducible across 11+ separate attempts from 06:43 to 07:07 (pids 18179, 18232, 19894, 20364, 20680, 25360, 32528, 32614, 7633, 13467, 13640, 14171, 14434, 14971). Initially misdiagnosed by the assistant as a generic device/memory-pressure 'crash' -- logcat evidence corrected this. KEY ISOLATING FACT: a standalone `test-backend-ops -b HTP0` run with only small synthetic matrices (examples/npu-matrix-cases.txt, no real model) passed clean (8/8 OK, no abort) right after the ADSP_LIBRARY_PATH fix. The corruption appears specifically when the real model's tensors (qwen3next: MoE MUL_MAT_ID + hybrid full-attention/linear-recurrent layers) run through the experimental Hexagon backend -- not a RAM-capacity issue tunable via batch size.
failed_attempts.hardware_context: S24 Ultra, 10GiB total RAM. Not fixed by reducing -ngl, -b/-ub, or any resource knob tried -- this is being treated as a likely memory-safety bug in ggml-hexagon.cpp (explicitly logged as 'Hexagon backend (experimental)') when combined with this architecture, not a tuning problem.
failed_attempts.do_not_repeat: RESOLVED 2026-10-08T07:40Z: root cause found and fixed, see completed_steps. ggml-hexagon.cpp:7517 hardcodes mmap_support=false; llama-model.cpp's AUTO load-mode logic disables mmap for the entire model when any -dev device lacks mmap support, forcing an eager full-8.4GB-file read that exhausted RAM in ~10s. The earlier Scudo 'invalid chunk state' aborts were almost certainly a symptom of this same RSS explosion, not a separate memory-safety bug. FIX: always pass -lm mmap (--load-mode mmap) explicitly whenever -dev HTP0 is used -- this bypasses the AUTO-only check and was verified live (full logcat+mem-monitor+watchdog instrumentation) to run cleanly with stable memory (free 650-760MB, available pinned 5.5GB throughout, peak process RSS ~6.1GB, zero crashes, zero Scudo errors).
